messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: network-lb-health-high for prod-edge-us-east-1. Severity: P1. page_id=PD-4472. Targets unhealthy > 60%

pagerduty: Page fired to sam (oncall) and priya; escalation in 5m if not acknowledged.

sam (oncall): acked. I'm on it. starting checks.

priya: thx. i'm hopping in — will check Route53 and certs.

sam (oncall): quick summary from dashboards: front-proxy 5xx spike, ALB target_healthy_count dropped from 120 -> 38 in ~2m. connection errors show TLS handshake failures 525 from edge.

maria (sre): seeing same in metrics. Cloudwatch -> ALB: TargetHealthDescription: TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE on several targets. Logs show repeated 'received fatal alert: handshake_failure'.

sam (oncall): running health check query:
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --region us-east-1
```
returns many `unhealthy (TLS handshake)` entries.

priya: checking DNS TTLs — nothing changed recently, Route53 records still pointing to ALB primary (ttl 60). No deploys in last 30m according to deploy-bot.

devon: support queue seeing customer errors: support-bot flagged 18 customers with elevated error rates. Tickets #3421-3428 correlated to region us-east-1.

sam (oncall): tentative impact: partial traffic to prod-edge failing TLS, fallback route to secondary region healthy for some users. Not total outage but severe latency/errors for clients hitting affected AZ.

priya: certs: checked cert-manager and ACM — certs valid, not expired. Fingerprints match.

maria (sre): collecting per-host logs, looks like OpenSSL negotiation failing with TLS1.3 chacha fallback on some older drivers. Might be a kernel-level update mismatch on a few hosts. Host list: i-0a1b2c3d, i-0f4e5d6c, i-09a8b7c6.

sam (oncall): rolling restart of affected target group nodes? If it's TLS library mismatch, restarting should pick up the correct config. I'll drain and restart 3 at a time.

priya: before we restart, can we fail traffic to the warm standby LB in us-west-2 for affected customers? Lower blast radius. If we change Route53 weight to send 30% traffic to us-west-2, we can reduce pressure.

sam (oncall): good idea. Changing weights now.

sam (oncall): Route53 change submitted: set prod-edge-weighted record -> us-east-1:70, us-west-2:30. Propagation in ~60s (ttl 60). Command:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://weighted.json --hosted-zone-id Z3EXAMPLE
```

devon: support-bot: posting customer notice draft to status page for review.

support-bot: Draft status update posted to internal channel. Suggested text: "We are investigating elevated TLS errors affecting a subset of traffic in US-EAST-1. Mitigation in progress; failover to secondary region underway."

priya: I can confirm some clients stop erroring after switching to us-west-2 in our logs (gateway-client-ip samples). Weighted failover helping.

sam (oncall): starting rolling restart on target-group prod-edge-tg-1. Draining host i-0a1b2c3d -> restart -> verify.

maria (sre): while restarting, noticed kernel patch rolled out automatically on a few hosts ~1h ago via our auto-update. That aligns with symptom window. I'll open a change blocker to hold updates until we patch template.

sam (oncall): first host back, health -> healthy. TLS handshake errors for that host stopped. Good sign. Continuing in batches.

priya: routing metrics: 5xxs down 45% since weight change + first batch restart. Still not fully recovered.

devon: PagerDuty: escalation suppressed after ack. Leaving notes on PD incident: "rolling restarts + weighted DNS failover in progress; kernel rollout suspected."

sam (oncall): second batch done. Target healthy count now 110/120. Incremental improvement.

maria (sre): I isolated package `openssl-3.0.8-1` as the common delta on rebooted hosts vs failing hosts. Patch candidate: recompile with updated shim or roll back. Let's keep rolling restarts for now.

priya: I'll coordinate with infra to freeze auto-updates. Filing FR: infra-change-2878.

sam (oncall): traffic metrics look stable. Error rate down to near baseline after last batch. Continuing monitoring for 15m.

devon: support-bot pushed customer-facing status update to status.redwood.ai: "Partial impact to traffic in us-east-1; mitigation in progress. No data loss. Engineers actively remediating."

support-bot: Updated customers notified: 22 affected accounts (emails queued).

sam (oncall): handing off to priya for night coverage. My shift ends in 20m. Current state: degraded -> recovering, healthy targets 118/120, route53 weighted to 70/30, restart plan completed.

priya: taking over. I'll keep PD incident open but change severity to P2 for watch. Will follow up with post-incident writeup.

maria (sre): created a short runbook note in incident doc: causes suspected = auto kernel/openssl rollout; mitigation = rolling restarts, route53 weighted failover, freeze auto-updates. Follow-ups: audit auto-update policy, bake patch, add health-check TLS fallback path.

priya: acknowledged. Paging out to infra to revert auto-update config and schedule a maintenance window for controlled patching tomorrow. @devon please confirm support messaging cadence.

devon: confirmed — support will send final customer update in 2h with root-cause summary when we have it.

sam (oncall): thanks team. leaving notes on PD and ops.

pagerduty: Incident PD-4472 acknowledged and assigned to priya. No further escalations scheduled.

priya: closing chat—moving to monitoring. will post RCA draft tomo. :white_check_mark:
